definition: Great man theory is an individualistic view of history that explains historical change mainly through the influence of outstanding persons or geniuses. In this account, major events are understood chiefly by what exceptional individuals do rather than by broader social or environmental forces.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Historyp; pinned source text

reasons: The packet supports only that “Great Man theory” is an “Individualistic (Lehmann)” interpretation within a classification of theories of history, but it does not state the definition’s claims that it explains historical change mainly through “outstanding persons or geniuses.”

The packet does not explicitly contrast the Great Man theory with “broader social or environmental forces,” nor does it describe major events as chiefly explained by what exceptional individuals do rather than other forces.

The packet supports Great man theory as an individualistic interpretation of history, but it does not directly support the stronger claim that it explains historical change mainly through “outstanding persons or geniuses.”

The packet contrasts Great man theory with environment-based accounts, but it does not clearly support the broader explanatory wording that major events are understood chiefly by exceptional individuals rather than broader social or environmental forces.
